title: Integration, business apps, developer tools, end-user computing, web/mobile, IoT and support
learningObjective: Choose the right service for messaging and notifications, business applications, business support, developing and troubleshooting applications, delivering desktops/apps to end users, building web and mobile front ends, and managing IoT devices.
foundation: Application integration: Amazon SNS sends notifications to many subscribers, Amazon SQS queues messages between components, Amazon EventBridge routes events between services.
Business apps: Amazon Connect for contact centers, Amazon SES for email.

Developer tools: AWS CodeBuild, AWS CodePipeline, AWS X-Ray. End-user computing: Amazon WorkSpaces, Amazon AppStream 2.0, Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser. Front end: AWS Amplify. IoT: AWS IoT Core. Help: AWS Support plans.
engineer: SNS (pub/sub, push to email, SMS, HTTP, Lambda, SQS; fan-out), SQS (standard and FIFO queues, decoupling, buffering), EventBridge (event bus, rules, scheduler, SaaS integrations), Step Functions (workflow orchestration).
Amazon Connect (omnichannel cloud contact center), Amazon SES (transactional and marketing email, inbound email processing).
CodeBuild (managed builds/tests), CodePipeline (release pipelines), X-Ray (distributed tracing and service maps). AWS CLI, CodeDeploy and Cloud9-style tooling also support development.
WorkSpaces (persistent virtual desktops), AppStream 2.0 (stream individual desktop applications to a browser), WorkSpaces Secure Browser (managed browser for internal websites and SaaS).
AWS Amplify (build, connect and host full-stack web and mobile apps), AWS IoT Core (connect devices securely with MQTT, rules engine).
Business support options: AWS Support plans (Basic plus paid plans), AWS re:Post, AWS Professional Services, partners; see task 4.3 for detail.

example.title: An event-driven retailer
body: Orders go into an SQS queue processed by workers; failures publish to an SNS topic that emails and texts the on-call team; EventBridge rules trigger fraud checks. Builds run in CodeBuild through CodePipeline and X-Ray traces slow calls. Store staff use WorkSpaces; the mobile app is built with Amplify; warehouse sensors connect through IoT Core.

prerequisites: An AWS account (use an IAM Identity Center user, not root)
permissions: Read-only access to explore; least-privilege permissions to change resources
limits: Conceptual objective: explore in the console; no configuration limits are tested

misconceptions.myth: SNS stores messages for later processing.
misconceptions.reality: SNS pushes; SQS stores messages until consumed.
It streams applications; WorkSpaces provides desktops.

architectureDecisions: Use SQS for decoupling, SNS for fan-out notifications, EventBridge for event routing.

AWS Amplify for web and mobile

steps.label: Busy order
steps.title: An order must trigger five things
body: When a customer orders: charge the card, update stock, email a receipt, alert the warehouse, and survive a 10x spike on sale days.
If one part is slow, the others shouldn't fail.

steps.label: SQS
steps.title: SQS: a queue between parts
body: Amazon SQS is a message queue. The web app drops the order in the queue and returns at once, and the order service takes messages at its own pace.
If the order service is down for a minute, nothing is lost. This is called decoupling.

steps.label: SNS + EventBridge
steps.title: SNS fans out; EventBridge routes events
body: Amazon SNS is publish/subscribe: one message goes to many subscribers at once (queues, Lambda, email, SMS). It's great for alerts and notifications.
Amazon EventBridge is an event bus. Rules match events from your apps, AWS services or SaaS and send them to targets. It also runs schedules.

callout.text: Queue for one consumer at its own pace = SQS. Push to many subscribers = SNS. Route events by rules = EventBridge.

steps.label: Business apps
steps.title: Email customers, answer calls
body: Amazon SES sends transactional and marketing email, such as order receipts.
Amazon Connect is a cloud contact center for customer calls and chats, with no phone hardware to buy.

steps.label: Dev tools
steps.title: Ship and debug the code
body: AWS CodePipeline automates the release steps from commit to production. AWS CodeBuild compiles and tests the code.
AWS X-Ray traces each request through your services so you can see which part is slow or failing.

steps.label: Amplify
steps.title: Build the frontend with Amplify
body: AWS Amplify helps build and host web and mobile frontends and connect them to backends for sign-in, APIs and storage, with CI/CD from your Git repository.

steps.label: Desktops + IoT
steps.title: Desktops for staff, sensors in the warehouse
body: Amazon WorkSpaces gives staff virtual desktops. Amazon AppStream 2.0 streams single apps to a browser. WorkSpaces Secure Browser gives a managed browser for internal web apps.
AWS IoT Core connects and manages the warehouse's sensors and scanners.

callout.text: Stuck? AWS Support plans, from Basic to Enterprise, are how you get business and technical help.
